jars: the 'room of forty people' metaphor in the mirror, which sounds like a poorly translated idiom and makes no sense
the Ramcharitmanas verse about 'advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you' being applied to his Toronto Uber life
the Day 7 story of Sita being abandoned in the forest, which frames his wife's crying as 'the cost of a road you chose together'
the instruction in the Day 1 audio to 'name the other four causes of this hard season out loud to yourself tonight, as you drive' — which is dangerously distracting
best: You are one cause among five. Your worth was never theirs to cut down, and the grief you feel for the present you cannot give back is real, but it is not the whole story.
day1_verdict: This verse actually names the exact trap I've been in — thinking my one choice ruined everything — and the 'five causes' idea is a relief because it means I'm not the sole author of this mess.
